clue.text: Churchman's book begun by one

parts.note: a cardinal is a senior churchman of the Roman Catholic Church; the possessive adds no letters
Numbers is the fourth book of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A clergyman's volume whose first chapter was written by someone else.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: the counting series one, two, three... is literally begun by one.
explanation.definitionFit: The ordinary counting numbers start their sequence at one, so the series is begun by one.

clue.text: Red port?

definitions.meaning: red in the face, as when blushing
The English name of Vlissingen, a Dutch seaport

explanation.definitionFit: Going red in the face is flushing, and Flushing is also a harbour town in the Netherlands.

clue.text: Irish saint from 25

indicators.note: the saint's name is made out of the letters of the other entry, rearranged

parts.note: the answer to 25-down, ADEN

explanation.surface: An Irish holy man who came from a port in Yemen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is the anagram signal: the four letters of the 25-down answer are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Enda of Aran was an early Irish monastic founder.

clue.text: Homes pronounced without hesitation to be of inferior quality

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: one word wraps around the other

parts.note: shlock (schlock) means cheap, shoddy goods
er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: Houses said quickly turn out to be poorly built.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking. The definition plays on the detective's surname Holmes, pronounced the same as homes.
explanation.definitionFit: Holmes, said aloud like homes, is the surname of the detective whose first name this is.

clue.text: Mark left by bit of monkey business?

parts.note: an imp is a little monkey in the sense of a small mischievous child
in theatre, business is a piece of stage action, an act

explanation.surface: A trace left behind after some mischief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'monkey business' looks like one phrase meaning mischief, but it splits into two pieces; a monkey here is a mischievous child.
explanation.definitionFit: An impact is the mark or effect left by something striking or influencing.

clue.text: Home organised to keep royal oil available — that's where it should stay

indicators.note: one group of letters keeps, or holds, the other inside it
the letters of Home are put into a new order
the oil and its companion letter are free to be rearranged

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for royal, as in RN or HRH

explanation.surface: Tidy the house and keep the royal oil to hand, since that is where it belongs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' rearranges Home into HEOM, and 'available' rearranges R plus oil into IRLO, which HEOM keeps inside. The definition leans on 'Home': a treasured family possession should stay in the family home.
explanation.definitionFit: A valued object passed down through generations is meant to stay in the family, never to be sold.

clue.text: 4 to order one tripe

parts.note: PO is a postal order
I is the Roman numeral for one
tripe is nonsense, rot

explanation.surface: A detective's instruction to arrange some offal.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition '4' means a detective like the 4-down answer. 'to order' looks like an anagram signal, but 'to' is a link and 'order' is PO, a postal order.
explanation.definitionFit: Agatha Christie's Belgian sleuth is a fictional detective, just like the famous Baker Street hero of 4-down.

clue.text: Novel with name one with novel

indicators.note: novel as an adjective means new, so these words are made anew

explanation.surface: A book featuring a name and a person who has a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' appears twice: first as the definition, then as the anagram signal meaning new.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilkie Collins wrote this 1859 mystery, an early example of detective fiction in novel form.

clue.text: Every bit of checked cotton fabric topped by creator of 17

parts.note: every bit means all

indicators.note: topped means having its head cut off, losing its first letter

parts.note: gingham is a cotton cloth woven in checks

explanation.surface: A designer covered head to toe in checked cotton material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topped' here means beheaded, not covered: GINGHAM loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Margery Allingham wrote the detective novels featuring the gentleman sleuth Albert Campion.

clue.text: Manage return getting hard time

indicators.note: return means the word for manage is turned round

parts.note: to manage is to cope
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Coping on your way back can be a hard time.
explanation.definitionFit: An epoch is an era, a long period of time.

clue.text: Black mood of the French couple

parts.note: des is French for of the (plural)
a couple is a pair

explanation.surface: A French couple in a dark frame of mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Despair is utter hopelessness, a black mood of the darkest kind.

clue.text: Fliers' 'aircut?

parts.note: a crew cut is a style of haircut; with the h dropped, as in Cockney speech

explanation.surface: A Cockney asks about the haircut favoured by pilots.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe marks a dropped H: haircut becomes 'aircut, and a crew cut gives AIR + CREW.
explanation.definitionFit: The team who fly and staff an aeroplane are its flying crew, the fliers.

clue.text: Name of someone I love

indicators.note: of signals that the name is a part taken from the words that follow

explanation.surface: The name of my beloved.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across someoNE I Love.
explanation.definitionFit: Neil is a common man's first name.

clue.text: Letters to me, Mister? Possibly, like most of our creators' work

definitions.text: like most of our creators' work

parts.note: letters delivered are the post

indicators.note: possibly says these letters might be arranged differently

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether letters addressed to him are for Mister.
explanation.walkthrough: The creators are the theme's crime writers: their stories revolve around examinations of corpses, and as all but one are dead, their books are now read after death.
explanation.definitionFit: Post-mortem means after death, and examinations of bodies fill crime fiction; most of the theme's authors are also dead.

clue.text: Motion of member (Labour)

parts.note: a leg is a limb, or member, of the body
labour is work

explanation.surface: A motion tabled by a Labour Party MP.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as Parliament: a motion from a Labour member. In fact a member is a LEG and labour is WORK.
explanation.definitionFit: Legwork is the walking and running about a task needs, hence physical motion.

clue.text: ? No, I choose good visibility

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as '? No, I choose good visibility' starts with a bare '?': the definition word is lost. The blog parses OPT + I + MIST (OPTIMIST, last letter unchecked), but the held answer is OPTIMISM and nothing in the clue as held defines either.

clue.text: Wild flower for winner out of hospital

indicators.note: the letter for hospital is taken out of the word for winner

parts.note: a winner is a champion

explanation.surface: Flowers bought for a victor just discharged from hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: Campion is also Margery Allingham's detective, which ties into the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Campion is a wild flowering plant of the pink family, such as red campion.

clue.text: About time — is Bond creator of 7?

parts.note: C is circa, Latin for about
hr is the abbreviation for hour, a unit of time
a tie is a bond

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether it is high time Bond's creator wrote a detective.
explanation.walkthrough: Bond suggests Ian Fleming, but it is just TIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Agatha Christie wrote the novels featuring the Belgian detective of 7-down.

clue.text: Little object going back to one state when hostile

indicators.note: going back means this word is read in reverse

parts.note: a mini is a small thing, as in a miniature
I is the Roman numeral for one
Cal is the abbreviation for California, a US state

explanation.surface: A tiny item returned to a single state that has turned unfriendly.
explanation.definitionFit: Inimical means unfriendly or harmful, the same as hostile.

clue.text: I turn early out of ordinary language

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of their order

explanation.surface: Someone decides to get up early and leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' looks like one phrase, but 'out' ends the anagram and 'of ordinary language' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Unliterary describes plain everyday speech, not the style of literature.

clue.text: Leaves alone, having you to follow?

definitions.meaning: the British call ... having you, a summons to get moving, puts having you after these two words

explanation.definitionFit: To let something be is to leave it alone, and the phrase starts the familiar call Let's be having you.

clue.text: Graded home for creator of 26

parts.note: to rank is to grade, place in order
in means at home

explanation.surface: A writer of graded homes.
explanation.walkthrough: Ian Rankin writes the novels about Inspector Rebus (26-across).
explanation.definitionFit: Ian Rankin created the Edinburgh police detective John Rebus.

clue.text: 13's given right of possession

indicators.note: given suggests the name is handed back, so it is read in reverse

parts.note: the answer to 13-across, the name NEIL

explanation.surface: A man named in another clue is granted rights of ownership.
explanation.walkthrough: The 13-across name read backwards gives the answer; it is also an anagram of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A lien is a legal right to keep someone's property until a debt is paid.

clue.text: It's on the road for a while, d'you hear, you chaps?

parts.note: a bit is a short while

indicators.note: d'you hear tells us the next word is to be taken as said, giving a letter

parts.note: you is said like the letter U
chaps are men

explanation.surface: A foreman tells his road crew they are tarring it for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitumen is the black tarry substance used to surface roads.

clue.text: God is within — don't speak the language

indicators.note: within says one group of letters is placed inside the other

parts.note: sh is the call for silence
Pan is the Greek god of the wild

explanation.surface: The god is inside, so keep quiet and say nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanish is the language of Spain and much of Latin America.

clue.text: A retreat into port

parts.note: a den is a private retreat

explanation.surface: Withdrawing into a harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Aden is a seaport in Yemen.

clue.text: Make another journey with a pictorial puzzle?

definitions.meaning: to ... is, whimsically, to take a bus again
a puzzle where pictures and letters stand for words

explanation.definitionFit: A rebus represents words by pictures; read as re-bus it is another bus ride. Rebus is also Rankin's detective.

clue.text: Journeying by train moving round point

indicators.note: round says the rearranged letters go around the point
moving says the letters of train are shifted

parts.note: a tine is a point or prong, as on a fork

explanation.surface: Travelling by a train that circles a point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' shuffles the letters of train into IRANT, which goes 'round' the point.
explanation.definitionFit: Itinerant means travelling from place to place, journeying.
